candidates.rawText:
Name : Y. K. SEHGAL

DOB : 29.04.1957

Educational/ professional qualification (along with the name of Institutions)

B.Sc(Engg) in Electrical Engineering, Delhi College of Engineering, Passed out in 1979

Nature of Experience (1)

Vast experience in various facets of Strategic Planning for overall development of power sector in general and transmission sector in particular

Developed the plan for national grid for scheme to achieve a target of 1,00,000 MW inter-regional capacity by 2016-17. These led to integration of NER, ER, WR and NR into one grid. This made the transfer of power more flexible and promoted trading of power from one corner of the country to the other.

Planning, development and implementation of high capacity Green Energy corridor 1 and Green Energy Corridor 2 for integration of Solar and Wind generation in the state of Tamil nadu, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Andhra pradesh , Maharashtra and Karnatka 

Planning & design studies for evaluation of techno-economical transmission systems for the entire capacity addition in the central sector and IPPs connected to ISTS.

Preparation of feasibility and detail project report including cost estimate for different transmission system involving high capacity AC lines and substaions. 

Contributed in efficient operation of transmission network and its high availability by active involvement in

Grid Operation Congestion Analysis

High Voltage and Under Voltage Analysis and remedial measures

Remedial measures for voltage and current unbalances on different phases

Voltage induction on de-energized circuits and means to control so as to perform maintenance works

Replacement of Circuit breaks with higher short circuit ratings to cater to increased fault levels under R&M policy

Switching Problems of 400kV Bus reactors & Swichable Line Reactors, Re-Setting of Distance Protection relays due to modified configuration of network on account of Series Compensation, System growth etc.

Relay Protection Setting of Transmissions Lines and Transformers.

Responsible for providing vital inputs for charging of new transmission networks

Reponsible for granting of Connectivity, Medium Term Open Access and Long Term Access to ISTS

Actively involved in implementation of smart grid

Actively involved in monitoring of pre-award implementation and corporate level management of all transmission schemes through close interaction with Region and Management.

Interaction with govt. departments/agencies , co-ordination with generating agencies for matching implementation of associated transmission system.

Coordination with CEA, Ministry of Power, STUs and other stakeholders for development and O&M related issues of transmission network.

Active participation in energy cooperation initiatives between India and neighboring countries like Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Afghanistan, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, etc.

Participated in meetings of BIMSTEC countries regarding harmonization of Grid Standards, formulation of Grid-interconnection Master Plan, drafting of MOU for implementation of Regional Power Trade Operating Agreement and establishment of BIMSTEC center of energy.

Provided inputs for tariff regulations, formulation of Indian Electricity Grid Code, Grid Standards, Open Access Regulations and Procedure.

Responsible for providing vital inputs for charging of new transmission networks

Responsible for granting of Long Term Access, Medium Term open access to ISTS system of CTU

Actively involved in implementation of smart grid

Co-ordination and interaction with different agencies related with power sector viz. MOP, CEA, CERC,SERCs,SEB, and IPPs for settlement of various transmission system related issues.

Actively associated with initiatives taken towards planning of interlinks and energy cooperation between India and neighbouring countries like Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Afghanistan, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Thailand etc.

.

Actively involved in formulation of open Access regulations, sharing regulations, tariff regulations, formulation of Indian Electricity Grid Code, Grid Standards, Open Access Regulations Procedures. 

Involved in evolving POC mechanism for sharing regulation and also its amendment in 2016.

Preparation and analysis of report for PSDF funding of NER – Agra High capacity HVDC link on the direction of CERC.

PUBLICATIONS

1. “Development of 1200kV Transmission System in India”, International Conf. for Development of 1200kV UHV AC Technology in India, 2010

2. “Planning and design studies for +800kV, 6000 MW HVDC system” CIGRE, Paris, 2008

3. “Testing of TCSC Damping Controller installed in a Tie Line Interconnecting Two Large Areas – A Case Study”, CIGRE, Paris 2006.

4. “Optimisation of Neutral Grounding Reactor Parameters – An Analysis for a Double circuit EHV line” IEEE Power India Conference, 2006.

5. “EHV Transmission Line Capacity Enhancement through increase in Surge Impedance Loading Level” IEEE Power India Conference, 2006.

6. “AC/DC Interaction in Multi-infeed HVDC scheme: A case Study” IEEE Power India Conference 2006.

7 “Change in Approach to Planning and Operation of Power Systems under Open Access Regime – Indian Experience” – St. Petersburg Power Tech’2005 Russia

8. “Application of FACTS Devices in Indian Power System”, CIGRE Colloquium Bangalore, 2005.

9. “Radical Performance Improvement – A Road map through technological innovation”. Power HP Forum, India 2005.

10. “Series capacitor project for 420kV Raipur-Fourkela line” Capacit 2005, IEEMA Conference, 2005.

11. “Series compensation on 400kV Transmission line – A few design aspects, 13th National Power System conference, Chennai, 2004.

12. “Application of emerging technologies for the development of Indian Power System, 19th World Energy Congress, Sydney, 2004.

13. “765kV system of Sipat power project in India”, International conference on Power System, Kathmandu, 2004.

14. “Emerging technologies and IT application in future Indian Power System”, International conference on IT application in Power System, India, 2003.

15. “Search for Optimal Technological Option for Power System Expansion in India – A Great Challenge”, CIGRE Symposium, Malaysia, 1999

 Experience in Commercial and Business Development Activities. Responsible for policy advocacy related to Ministry of POWER, CEA and CERC. Coordination with Ministry of POWER, MNRE, CEA, CTU , State utilities and CERC for new policies/ regulations suitable for new Energy transition Regime of Green Power. Coordination and interaction with different Central bidding agencies like SECI , NTPC and States. 

 Coordination with MOP and CEA and CERC for storage policy, regulations suitable for Electric storage and addressing issues for making viable the Electric storage in the country.

12. Detailed Tasks Assigned 
(i) Coordinate the preparation of the ESIA at national level in coordination with the
international ESIA coordinator/environmental, biodiversity and social experts to ensure
that the report meets all the TOR requirements (including the ESIA requirements in
Appendices A and B) in terms of content, time and quality as well as documenting project
conformance with ADB's Safeguard Policy Statement (2009) and government requirements.
(ii) Coordinate with the technical team to ensure appropriate technical input into the ESIA and
consideration of environmental and social criteria including technical design measures and
alternatives to avoid and or minimize the environmental and social (resettlement) impacts
as much as possible, in making final project design decisions.
(iii) Lead on identifying the environmental and social administrative framework, policy,
guidelines, laws and regulations applicable to the hydropower project and supporting
DGPC to obtain the statutory clearances in relation to the environment and social safeguards.

13. Work Undertaken that Best Illustrates Capability to Handle the Tasks Assigned

Name of assignment or project: Environment Impact Assessment of Pasakha Industrial Estate
Year: 2003-2004
Location: Pasakha, Chukha, Bhutan
Client: Royal Government of Bhutan
Main project features: Establishment of the First Industrial Estate in Bhutan.
Positions held: Environment Expert and of Air Pollution Dispersion Model Developer.
Activities performed: Collection of baseline data, identifying potential industries for location in the Industrial Estate, development of dispersion model to predict probable environmental impacts including cross-border pollution, establishing estate specific emission and discharge standards, alternative analysis, development of mitigation and monitoring plan.

Name of assignment or project: ESIA of Punatsangchhu-I and II Hydroelectric Projects
Year: 2005-2007
Location: wangduephodrang, Bhutan
Client: Government of India and Royal Government of Bhutan 
Main project features: Construction of two mega projects including the construction of dam, desilting arrangements, head-race-tunnels, power house complexes, housing colony and contractor site facilities.
Positions held: Sr. Environment Officer (MoEA) and Baseline Data Collection (EIA Team). 
Activities performed: Collection of baseline environmental information including ambient air quality, water quality, flora & fauna including aquatic and benthic biota. Assessment of potential environmental impacts and development of environment management and mitigation plan. 

Name of assignment or project: Sustainable Land Management Project
Year: 2005
Location:Zhemgang, Bhutan
Client: Minsitry of Agriculture, Bhutan
Main project features: Instituting sustainable land management practices in the agriculture, mining and forestry sector including capacity building of farmers, governmetn officials and business communities.
Positions held: Environment and Social Development Expert.
Activities performed: Reviewed the World Bank Environment and Social Management Framework and identified potential environmental and social impacts which would be considered significant. Developed environmental and social safeguards to comply with World Bank and Global Environment Facility requirements. 

Name of assignment or project: Revision of EIA Report of Punatsangchhu-II Hydroelectric Project (PHEP-II).
Year: 2011
Location: Wangduephodrang, Bhutan
Client: PHPA-II (Govt. Of India and Government of Bhutan.
Main project features: Construction of 1020 MW mega project including the construction of dam, desilting arrangements, head-race-tunnels, power house complex, housing colony and contractor site facilities. 
Positions held: Dy. Chief Environment Officer and Team Leader
Activities performed: Updated the EIA report of Punatsangchhu-II Hydroelectric Project focusing on the need to determine E-flow requirements and development of mitigation measures to protect the critically endangered white bellied heron and the golden mahseer.Coordinated the work of the team of experts from the government of Bhutan and the government of India to ensure that the updated EIA report complies with the statutory requirements of the two governments as well as the criteria for registration as a CDM Project. Developed special safeguard mechanisms pertaining to the impact of ground vibrations from the use of explosives on buildings and irrigation channels and instituted a robust monitoring mechanism.

Name of assignment or project: Implementation of the Environment Management Plan of PHEP-II. 
Year: 2011-2016
Location: Wangduephodrang, Bhutan
Client: PHPA-II
Main project features: Implementing the Environment Management and Mitigation Plan and quarterly progress report on compliance monitoring to the National Environment Commission.
Positions held: Dy. Chief and Chief Environment Officer
Activities performed: Voluntary compliance monitoring and reporting, Implementing environment and social safeguards including the land aquisition and compensation, construction of the WBH Conservation Centre (in collaboration with the Royal Society for the Protection of Nature), Construction of the Golden Mahseer Hatchery and Conservation Center (in collaboration with the National Center for Cold Water and Riverine Fisheries), processing for environmental clearances and development consents for various works not covered under the ESIA. Developing the Project Design Document, obtaining Host country approvals (Govt of Bhutan and Govt of India), applying for registration as CDM projects for both PHEP-I and PHEP-II (PHEP-I is registered as a CDM project while registration of PHEP-II was under process).

Name of assignment or project: EIA of Jigmeling, Matonga and Dhamdhum Industrial Parks.
Year: 2016-17
Location: Gelephu, Samdrupjongkhar and Samtse
Client: Govt. Of Bhutan
Main project features: Construction of Industrial Parks in the Southern region of Bhutan.
Positions held: Chief Environment Officer/ Team Leader, EIA
Activities performed: Compilation of legal and policy gudielines framework for the conduct of ESIA, formulation of ToR for the ESIA of the three industrial parks, selection of consultants, supervising the ESIA process and report compilation, obtaining approvals from the then National Environment Commission (NEC).

Name of assignment or project: Optimization and Augmentation of the Lhaki Steel and Rolling Mills.
Year: 2017

Activities Performed: Reviewed the Contractor’s environment management plan (EMP), and report to DoE, reviewed progress on EMP implementation and made the required corrections as the Contractor’s work progresses, initiated and conducted inquiries and prepared reports, following any incidents of violations, that have local or regional impacts, led all introductory and ongoing training of the Contractor staff, PMC staff, DRE staff and visitors, to the project site, and led training on environment management for DoE and other staff taking-over power plants and internal transmission lines, to ensure that the Contractor adhere to all the provisions in the Environment Management Plan (EMP), reported any violations to ESS as appropriate and assisted in implementing solutions and remedial measures, coordinated the implementation of the grievance redressal mechanism and assist DoE to resolve on-going issues of environmental, social and health impacts during construction.

Name of Project: Skills Training and Education Pathways Upgradation Project.

Month and Year: February 2022 to October 2024 (Intermittent)

Location: Bhutan

Client: ADB/MOESD

Main Project Features: To assess the environmental impact of the infrastructure works and prepare the bi-annual and annual environmental monitoring report for the infrastructure components of the STEP-UP project.

Position Held: Environmental Monitoring Expert(Environment, social & OHS)

Activities Performed: Obtained copies of and review the requirements of the IEE including EMP plus grant agreement and project administration manual (PAM), as disclosed on the ADB’s website, to gain a thorough understanding of the project’s environment safeguard requirements.; work with the PMU and their contractors, seek and review relevant documentation prepared by contractors on implementation of environmental safeguard requirements; conduct site visit to assess the current level of compliance with the environmental safeguard requirements including health and safety protocol; systematically document the status of the current level of compliance against an inventory of environment safeguard requirements (compliance to ADB safeguard policy, national regulations, EMP); collect information on the environmental monitoring (air quality and noise measurements). This must be budgeted under the project costs; assess whether any grievances have been recorded and actions taken by the contractors and/or PMU; informed by the findings, the consultant will prepare the required EMR and submit these to the PMU. The EMR must include summary of findings and recommended corrective actions required if any; and support PMU in collecting relevant environmental safeguard related documents for new skills development projects.

Month and Year: November 2018 to February 2024 (Intermittent)

Location: Sarpang, Samdrup Jongkhar and Trashigang, Bhutan

Client: ADB/Department of Infrastructure Development, MoIT, Bhutan

Main Project Features: Provide monitoring and supervision to assist the Royal Government of Bhutan in the efficient and effective implementation of the Secondary Towns Urban Development Project (STUDP)

Position Held: PMSC Environment Specialist (Environment & OHS)

Activities Performed:

Ensured that all ADB and/or RGoB social, safeguard and environment regulations/statutory requirements and related issues are properly incorporated into the design and implementation phases of the project, carried out environmental safeguards due diligence appropriate to the proposed project and prepare/ update necessary safeguard documents.

Undertook the reporting requirements of the projects encompassing all the statutory requirements of the ADB and/or the Government,

Developed a grievance redressal mechanism and dispute resolution mechanism as and when they arise,

Ensured and monitored implementation of the project, carried out by the PIU,

Developed the M&E framework and conduct project monitoring as agreed with ADB in the project performance management system (PPMS),

Developed/Revised Initial environmental examination (IEE) reports including associated environmental management plans (EMP) based on detailed design and ensure these are included in bidding and contract documents, and

Prepared the semi-annual environmental monitoring reports to be submitted to ADB.

Month and Year: September 2016 to May 2018

Location: Phuentsholing, Chukha, Bhutan

Client: UNDP/Phuentsholing Thromde, Bhutan

Main Project Features: Provide construction supervision, environment management and monitoring of landslides stabilization works under taken by contractors at Rinchending check post, Reldri School, Rinchending Goenpa and old hospital areas.

Position Held: Environmental/Bioengineering Specialist 

Activities Performed: Advise contractors in all matters covering safety and care of work, environmental management, organize meetings at site regarding progress, plan, labour, quality assurance, quality control and specifications, prepare and issue site visit report to Phuentsholing Thromde, ensure compliance with the environment and social safeguards of civil works contract, provide on –job or on-site advice and training to site contractors where necessary and ensure safety working procedures, and Environmental Mitigation Plan and the Monitoring Plan is properly adhered.

Name of Project: To provide independent advisory and consulting services to THyE in the field of Environmental management Plan for implementation of 118 MW Nikachhu Hydropower Project

Month and Year: February 2014 to June 2024 (Quarterly)

Location: Tangsibji, Trongsa

Client: Tangsibji Hydro Energy Limited (THyE)

Main Project Features: To provide independent advisory and consulting services to THyE in the field of Environmental management Plan for implementation of 118 MW Nikachhu Hydropower Project, monitoring the implementation of environmental impact and mitigation measures outlined in the Environmental Management Plan of 118MW Nikachhu Hydropower Project and advise on any other matter deemed important by THyE.

Position Held: Panel of Expert(Environment & OHS)

Activities Performed: Review implementation of plans to determine if this fully compile with ADB safeguards and assess appropriateness of provisions in mitigation measures, monitoring plan, budget, institutional arrangements and compliance mechanisms; determine if the EMP provisions for mitigation and monitoring are being implemented properly by THyE and DGPC, all contractors and consultants; conduct site visits to assess the performance of THyE and DGPC andthe contractors in implementation of environmental mitigation and monitoring measures specified in the EMP, consult with relevant stakeholders during field visits, record their concerns and expectations and develop recommendations to address valid concerns; determine if the EMP (for all project phases) is fully funded and if funding sources have been identified and committed; comment on cumulative nature of impacts-both impacts that result from projects and those exerted on the project from other sources; recommend corrective actions in case environmental mitigation measures are not sufficient and/or considered to deviate from requirements of Bhutan’s and ADB’s safeguard policies; assess adequacy of baseline surveys and analysis and determine need to collect additional baseline data; examine monitoring program designed for construction and operation phases to determine appropriateness of objectives and activities to current and predicted project impacts and recommend revision and /or additional components as necessary; examine and recommend current institutional capacity of environmental and social management unit within THyE/DGPC to address environmental safeguards if any; review time schedule for environmental mitigation programs and assess appropriateness of schedule for effective implementation and in compliance Bhutan’s and ADB’s safeguards policies; assess operation of grievance redress mechanism (GRM) for dispute resolution and recommend to redress areas not conforming to ADB safeguards and Government environmental regulations; assess any environmental issue if questioned by THyE, DGPC, the Government and financier( s) if questioned; facilitate and mediate with THyE, DGPC and financier(s) to resolve any social issues which has not been resolved by GRM; propose any actions in consultation with other PoE member( s) and other project stakeholders on any specific environmental issues which arise before or during project implementation; and share findings and knowledge with THyE and DGPC, government and/or financiers on environmental impacts and mitigation measures if required.

candidates.rawText:
Name : Y. K. SEHGAL

DOB : 29.04.1957

Educational/ professional qualification (along with the name of Institutions)

B.Sc(Engg) in Electrical Engineering, Delhi College of Engineering, Passed out in 1979

Nature of Experience (1)

Vast experience in various facets of Strategic Planning for overall development of power sector in general and transmission sector in particular

Developed the plan for national grid for scheme to achieve a target of 1,00,000 MW inter-regional capacity by 2016-17. These led to integration of NER, ER, WR and NR into one grid. This made the transfer of power more flexible and promoted trading of power from one corner of the country to the other.

Planning, development and implementation of high capacity Green Energy corridor 1 and Green Energy Corridor 2 for integration of Solar and Wind generation in the state of Tamil nadu, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Andhra pradesh , Maharashtra and Karnatka 

Planning & design studies for evaluation of techno-economical transmission systems for the entire capacity addition in the central sector and IPPs connected to ISTS.

Preparation of feasibility and detail project report including cost estimate for different transmission system involving high capacity AC lines and substaions. 

Contributed in efficient operation of transmission network and its high availability by active involvement in

Grid Operation Congestion Analysis

High Voltage and Under Voltage Analysis and remedial measures

Remedial measures for voltage and current unbalances on different phases

Voltage induction on de-energized circuits and means to control so as to perform maintenance works

Replacement of Circuit breaks with higher short circuit ratings to cater to increased fault levels under R&M policy

Switching Problems of 400kV Bus reactors & Swichable Line Reactors, Re-Setting of Distance Protection relays due to modified configuration of network on account of Series Compensation, System growth etc.

Relay Protection Setting of Transmissions Lines and Transformers.

Responsible for providing vital inputs for charging of new transmission networks

Reponsible for granting of Connectivity, Medium Term Open Access and Long Term Access to ISTS

Actively involved in implementation of smart grid

Actively involved in monitoring of pre-award implementation and corporate level management of all transmission schemes through close interaction with Region and Management.

Interaction with govt. departments/agencies , co-ordination with generating agencies for matching implementation of associated transmission system.

Coordination with CEA, Ministry of Power, STUs and other stakeholders for development and O&M related issues of transmission network.

Active participation in energy cooperation initiatives between India and neighboring countries like Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Afghanistan, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, etc.

Participated in meetings of BIMSTEC countries regarding harmonization of Grid Standards, formulation of Grid-interconnection Master Plan, drafting of MOU for implementation of Regional Power Trade Operating Agreement and establishment of BIMSTEC center of energy.

Provided inputs for tariff regulations, formulation of Indian Electricity Grid Code, Grid Standards, Open Access Regulations and Procedure.

Responsible for providing vital inputs for charging of new transmission networks

Responsible for granting of Long Term Access, Medium Term open access to ISTS system of CTU

Actively involved in implementation of smart grid

Co-ordination and interaction with different agencies related with power sector viz. MOP, CEA, CERC,SERCs,SEB, and IPPs for settlement of various transmission system related issues.

Actively associated with initiatives taken towards planning of interlinks and energy cooperation between India and neighbouring countries like Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Afghanistan, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Thailand etc.

.

Actively involved in formulation of open Access regulations, sharing regulations, tariff regulations, formulation of Indian Electricity Grid Code, Grid Standards, Open Access Regulations Procedures. 

Involved in evolving POC mechanism for sharing regulation and also its amendment in 2016.

Name of Project: Project Management Consultants to implement EMP for environmental and social safeguards compliance for construction of Sephu Solar Power Project

Month and Year: September 2023 to June 2025 (Intermittent)

Location: Sephu, Wangdue Phodrang, Bhutan

Client: Department of Energy/ADB

Main Project Features: Review the Contractor’s environment management plan (EMP), progress on EMP implementation and make the required corrections, initiate and conduct inquiries and prepare reports, lead all introductory and ongoing training of the Contractor staff, PMC staff, DoE staff and visitors, to the project site, and lead training on environment management for DoE and other staff taking-over power plants and internal transmission lines, to ensure that the Contractor adhere to all the provisions in the Environment Management Plan (EMP), report any violations to ESS as appropriate and assist in implementing solutions and remedial measures, coordinate the implementation of the grievance redressal mechanism and assist DoE to resolve on-going issues of environmental, social and health impacts during construction.

Position Held: Senior Environmental Expert (Environment, social &OHS)

Activities Performed: Reviewed the Contractor’s environment management plan (EMP), and report to DoE, reviewed progress on EMP implementation and made the required corrections as the Contractor’s work progresses, initiated and conducted inquiries and prepared reports, following any incidents of violations, that have local or regional impacts, led all introductory and ongoing training of the Contractor staff, PMC staff, DRE staff and visitors, to the project site, and led training on environment management for DoE and other staff taking-over power plants and internal transmission lines, to ensure that the Contractor adhere to all the provisions in the Environment Management Plan (EMP), reported any violations to ESS as appropriate and assisted in implementing solutions and remedial measures, coordinated the implementation of the grievance redressal mechanism and assist DoE to resolve on-going issues of environmental, social and health impacts during construction.

Name of Project: Skills Training and Education Pathways Upgradation Project.

Month and Year: February 2022 to October 2024 (Intermittent)

Location: Bhutan

Client: ADB/MOESD

Main Project Features: To assess the environmental impact of the infrastructure works and prepare the bi-annual and annual environmental monitoring report for the infrastructure components of the STEP-UP project.

Position Held: Environmental Monitoring Expert(Environment, social & OHS)

Activities Performed: Obtained copies of and review the requirements of the IEE including EMP plus grant agreement and project administration manual (PAM), as disclosed on the ADB’s website, to gain a thorough understanding of the project’s environment safeguard requirements.; work with the PMU and their contractors, seek and review relevant documentation prepared by contractors on implementation of environmental safeguard requirements; conduct site visit to assess the current level of compliance with the environmental safeguard requirements including health and safety protocol; systematically document the status of the current level of compliance against an inventory of environment safeguard requirements (compliance to ADB safeguard policy, national regulations, EMP); collect information on the environmental monitoring (air quality and noise measurements). This must be budgeted under the project costs; assess whether any grievances have been recorded and actions taken by the contractors and/or PMU; informed by the findings, the consultant will prepare the required EMR and submit these to the PMU. The EMR must include summary of findings and recommended corrective actions required if any; and support PMU in collecting relevant environmental safeguard related documents for new skills development projects. 

Name of Project: Project Management and Supervision Consultant for implementation of Secondary Towns Urban Development Project

Month and Year: November 2018 to February 2024 (Intermittent)

Location: Sarpang, Samdrup Jongkhar and Trashigang, Bhutan

Client: ADB/Department of Infrastructure Development, MoIT, Bhutan

Main Project Features: Provide monitoring and supervision to assist the Royal Government of Bhutan in the efficient and effective implementation of the Secondary Towns Urban Development Project (STUDP)

Position Held: PMSC Environment Specialist (Environment & OHS)

Activities Performed:

Ensured that all ADB and/or RGoB social, safeguard and environment regulations/statutory requirements and related issues are properly incorporated into the design and implementation phases of the project, carried out environmental safeguards due diligence appropriate to the proposed project and prepare/ update necessary safeguard documents.

Undertook the reporting requirements of the projects encompassing all the statutory requirements of the ADB and/or the Government,

Developed a grievance redressal mechanism and dispute resolution mechanism as and when they arise,

Ensured and monitored implementation of the project, carried out by the PIU,

Developed the M&E framework and conduct project monitoring as agreed with ADB in the project performance management system (PPMS),

Developed/Revised Initial environmental examination (IEE) reports including associated environmental management plans (EMP) based on detailed design and ensure these are included in bidding and contract documents, and

Prepared the semi-annual environmental monitoring reports to be submitted to ADB.

Name of Project: Supervision of land stabilization works under Phuentsholing Thromde (NAPA II Project)

Month and Year: September 2016 to May 2018

Location: Phuentsholing, Chukha, Bhutan

Client: UNDP/Phuentsholing Thromde, Bhutan

Main Project Features: Provide construction supervision, environment management and monitoring of landslides stabilization works under taken by contractors at Rinchending check post, Reldri School, Rinchending Goenpa and old hospital areas.

Position Held: Environmental/Bioengineering Specialist 

Activities Performed: Advise contractors in all matters covering safety and care of work, environmental management, organize meetings at site regarding progress, plan, labour, quality assurance, quality control and specifications, prepare and issue site visit report to Phuentsholing Thromde, ensure compliance with the environment and social safeguards of civil works contract, provide on –job or on-site advice and training to site contractors where necessary and ensure safety working procedures, and Environmental Mitigation Plan and the Monitoring Plan is properly adhered.

Name of Project: To provide independent advisory and consulting services to THyE in the field of Environmental management Plan for implementation of 118 MW Nikachhu Hydropower Project

Month and Year: February 2014 to June 2024 (Quarterly)

Location: Tangsibji, Trongsa

Client: Tangsibji Hydro Energy Limited (THyE)

Main Project Features: To provide independent advisory and consulting services to THyE in the field of Environmental management Plan for implementation of 118 MW Nikachhu Hydropower Project, monitoring the implementation of environmental impact and mitigation measures outlined in the Environmental Management Plan of 118MW Nikachhu Hydropower Project and advise on any other matter deemed important by THyE.

Position Held: Panel of Expert(Environment & OHS)

Activities Performed: Review implementation of plans to determine if this fully compile with ADB safeguards and assess appropriateness of provisions in mitigation measures, monitoring plan, budget, institutional arrangements and compliance mechanisms; determine if the EMP provisions for mitigation and monitoring are being implemented properly by THyE and DGPC, all contractors and consultants; conduct site visits to assess the performance of THyE and DGPC andthe contractors in implementation of environmental mitigation and monitoring measures specified in the EMP, consult with relevant stakeholders during field visits, record their concerns and expectations and develop recommendations to address valid concerns; determine if the EMP (for all project phases) is fully funded and if funding sources have been identified and committed; comment on cumulative nature of impacts-both impacts that result from projects and those exerted on the project from other sources; recommend corrective actions in case environmental mitigation measures are not sufficient and/or considered to deviate from requirements of Bhutan’s and ADB’s safeguard policies; assess adequacy of baseline surveys and analysis and determine need to collect additional baseline data; examine monitoring program designed for construction and operation phases to determine appropriateness of objectives and activities to current and predicted project impacts and recommend revision and /or additional components as necessary; examine and recommend current institutional capacity of environmental and social management unit within THyE/DGPC to address environmental safeguards if any; review time schedule for environmental mitigation programs and assess appropriateness of schedule for effective implementation and in compliance Bhutan’s and ADB’s safeguards policies; assess operation of grievance redress mechanism (GRM) for dispute resolution and recommend to redress areas not conforming to ADB safeguards and Government environmental regulations; assess any environmental issue if questioned by THyE, DGPC, the Government and financier( s) if questioned; facilitate and mediate with THyE, DGPC and financier(s) to resolve any social issues which has not been resolved by GRM; propose any actions in consultation with other PoE member( s) and other project stakeholders on any specific environmental issues which arise before or during project implementation; and share findings and knowledge with THyE and DGPC, government and/or financiers on environmental impacts and mitigation measures if required.

Expert’s contact information : [e-mail : khenrig@gmail.com]

Activities Performed: Obtained copies of and review the requirements of the IEE including EMP plus grant agreement and project administration manual (PAM), as disclosed on the ADB s website, to gain a thorough understanding of the project s environment safeguard requirements.; work with the PMU and their contractors, seek and review relevant documentation prepared by contractors on implementation of environmental safeguard requirements; conduct site visit to assess the current level of compliance with the environmental safeguard requirements including health and safety protocol; systematically document the status of the current level of compliance against an inventory of environment safeguard requirements (compliance to ADB safeguard policy, national regulations, EMP); collect information on the environmental monitoring (air quality and noise measurements). This must be budgeted under the project costs; assess whether any grievances have been recorded and actions taken by the contractors and/or PMU; informed by the findings, the consultant will prepare the required EMR and submit these to the PMU. The EMR must include summary of findings and recommended corrective actions required if any; and support PMU in collecting relevant environmental safeguard related documents for new skills development projects.

Prepared the semi-annual environmental monitoring reports to be submitted to ADB.

Position Held: Panel of Expert(Environment & OHS)
Activities Performed: Review implementation of plans to determine if this fully compile with ADB safeguards and assess appropriateness of provisions in mitigation measures, monitoring plan, budget, institutional arrangements and compliance mechanisms; determine if the EMP provisions for mitigation and monitoring are being implemented properly by THyE and DGPC, all contractors and consultants; conduct site visits to assess the performance of THyE and DGPC andthe contractors in implementation of environmental mitigation and monitoring measures specified in the EMP, consult with relevant stakeholders during field visits, record their concerns and expectations and develop recommendations to address valid concerns; determine if the EMP (for all project phases) is fully funded and if funding sources have been identified and committed; comment on cumulative nature of impacts-both impacts that result from projects and those exerted on the project from other sources; recommend corrective actions in case environmental mitigation measures are not sufficient and/or considered to deviate from requirements of Bhutan s and ADB s safeguard policies; assess adequacy of baseline surveys and analysis and determine need to collect additional baseline data; examine monitoring program designed for construction and operation phases to determine appropriateness of objectives and activities to current and predicted project impacts and recommend revision and /or additional components as necessary; examine and recommend current institutional capacity of environmental and social management unit within THyE/DGPC to address environmental safeguards if any; review time schedule for environmental mitigation programs and assess appropriateness of schedule for effective implementation and in compliance Bhutan s and ADB s safeguards policies; assess operation of grievance redress mechanism (GRM) for dispute resolution and recommend to redress areas not conforming to ADB safeguards and Government environmental regulations; assess any environmental issue if questioned by THyE, DGPC, the Government and financier( s) if questioned; facilitate and mediate with THyE, DGPC and financier(s) to resolve any social issues which has not been resolved by GRM; propose any actions in consultation with other PoE member( s) and other project stakeholders on any specific environmental issues which arise before or during project implementation; Mukesh Khanna

 

Executive Director (Retired on 30/04/2024), Power Grid Corporation of India Ltd

Held Executive leadership position with a Maharatna PSU and World’s 3rd largest Transmission Company

PROFESSIONAL PROFILE

Seasoned Transmission & Power Sector expert with more than 32 years of extensive experience and demonstrated history in Transmission Planning for National Grid, Renewable generation, development of regulatory regime including connectivity/LTA/GNA for conventional as well as renewable generation, Commercial, Regulatory, Policy, Legal, Contractual, Sectoral Reforms, Business Strategy & Development and Project Management side in Transmission Sector. Structured, negotiated and executed numerous partnership agreements. Effectiveness demonstrated in strategic transmission planning for growth and integration of 5 grids in India into one synchronous grid.

Strategized/ led /part of Policy making in key Sectoral reforms beginning from separation of Transmission to introduction of Open Access, Electricity Act 2003, Tariff Policy, NEP, ISTS planning, Private participation in ISTS, Regulations and procedures for LTA/MTOA & GNA grant, processing of connectivity/LTA applications and Calculation and Sharing of ISTS charges. 

Managed Revenue Assurance, Commercial Agreements, Tariff Petitions, Regulatory and Legal matters, Dispute resolution, Court cases, Regulatory petition management, License & approval for new business, Contractual & Commercial transaction, Project Management and Stakeholder Consultation.

Looked after commercial transaction, Regulatory and Legal matters of all India Interstate Transmission Billing, Collection and Disbursement of more than Rs 45,000 Crs annually covering > 50 Transmission Licensees and >100 Discoms and DICs 

Leader with motivational management style & reputation for building and retaining highly motivated teams.

Dealt > 100 Tariff Petitions for New Assets for Capital cost 50,000 Crs and > 400 Truing up Petition for Capital cost > Rs 2 lakh Crores.

Successfully handled critical litigations and disputes in APTEL/High Courts/Supreme Courts to end long pending issues mainly related to Outstanding Dues, Mismatch issues, Tariff disputes. 

Led team for grant of Regulatory approvals for Transmission projects for Renewables Generation, and Solar Power parks in India, High Capacity Corridors, New Business initiatives. 

Engineer to Chief General Manager, CTU Aug’91 to Sep’20

Educational/ professional qualification (along with the name of Institutions)

B.Sc(Engg) in Electrical Engineering, Delhi College of Engineering, Passed out in 1979

Nature of Experience (1)

Vast experience in various facets of Strategic Planning for overall development of power sector in general and transmission sector in particular

Developed the plan for national grid for scheme to achieve a target of 1,00,000 MW inter-regional capacity by 2016-17. These led to integration of NER, ER, WR and NR into one grid. This made the transfer of power more flexible and promoted trading of power from one corner of the country to the other.

Planning, development and implementation of high capacity Green Energy corridor 1 and Green Energy Corridor 2 for integration of Solar and Wind generation in the state of Tamil nadu, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Andhra pradesh , Maharashtra and Karnatka 

Planning & design studies for evaluation of techno-economical transmission systems for the entire capacity addition in the central sector and IPPs connected to ISTS.

Preparation of feasibility and detail project report including cost estimate for different transmission system involving high capacity AC lines and substaions. 

Contributed in efficient operation of transmission network and its high availability by active involvement in

Grid Operation Congestion Analysis

High Voltage and Under Voltage Analysis and remedial measures

Remedial measures for voltage and current unbalances on different phases

Voltage induction on de-energized circuits and means to control so as to perform maintenance works

Replacement of Circuit breaks with higher short circuit ratings to cater to increased fault levels under R&M policy

Switching Problems of 400kV Bus reactors & Switchable Line Reactors, Re-Setting of Distance Protection relays due to modified configuration of network on account of Series Compensation, System growth etc.

Relay Protection Setting of Transmissions Lines and Transformers.

Responsible for providing vital inputs for charging of new transmission networks

Reponsible for granting of Connectivity, Medium Term Open Access and Long Term Access to ISTS

Actively involved in implementation of smart grid

Actively involved in monitoring of pre-award implementation and corporate level management of all transmission schemes through close interaction with Region and Management.

Interaction with govt. departments/agencies , co-ordination with generating agencies for matching implementation of associated transmission system.

Coordination with CEA, Ministry of Power, STUs and other stakeholders for development and O&M related issues of transmission network.

Active participation in energy cooperation initiatives between India and neighboring countries like Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Afghanistan, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, etc.

Participated in meetings of BIMSTEC countries regarding harmonization of Grid Standards, formulation of Grid-interconnection Master Plan, drafting of MOU for implementation of Regional Power Trade Operating Agreement and establishment of BIMSTEC center of energy.

Provided inputs for tariff regulations, formulation of Indian Electricity Grid Code, Grid Standards, Open Access Regulations and Procedure.

Experienced engineering graduate specialized in project planning, project management, project scheduling, site management, vendor

ECOZEN SOLUTIONS PVT LTD., TRIPURA, INDIA

This also involves developing detailed plans that outline project task, timelines, resources, & milestones. In this current role I 
am handling three projects (PM KUSUM Scheme) at a time which requires a strict project schedule & daily strict monitoring of 
project task. A 14.8MW solar plant (rooftop & ground mounted) and PM Kusum B & C project (ground mounted) are majorly 
involved in this project schedule which needs accurate resource allocation & vendor mapping. 
 
Material Planning & Management: To ensure timely completion of project within deadline it is very important for me to 
coordinate with SCM team & procurement team to plan resources for site. This requires regular tracking of site warehouse 
inventory which requires a strict material management plan and also a set of emergency mitigation plan for unavoidable 
circumstances. 
 
Daily Progress Tracking & Vendor Mapping: In this current role I am responsible for preparing daily action tracker and 
mapping of vendors for project task. Every project in this schedule needs several micro scheduled activities whose progress can 
impact pre-determined project plan, so it is important for me to track all activities regularly to know about project progress. 
 
Project Team Management: A dedicated project team is constantly working under my guidance and I am also responsible for 
tracking their daily work plan. They are assigned with different project tasks which are tracked & monitored in order to know 
individual performance and also project progress. 
 
Client Management: In my current role I am also responsible for handling all government client for smooth execution of project 
and smooth process of invoice for billing purpose. I am also responsible for reporting project progress report to our client 
whenever asked. All the official meetings with client are assigned to me and I am responsible for data validation. State Data 
Management Portal is also assigned to me to handle, which integrates site data with MNRE portal for monitoring purpose. 
 
FENICE ENERGY, TRIPURA, INDIA 
Senior Project Engineer | Feb. 2021 to June. 2023

Project Planning & Scheduling: In this role I was involved in central planning & coordination team in order to 
handle all planning & scheduling of project work at site. In this role I have handled a 7.2MW (rooftop) solar project, 
a 15MW (rooftop & ground mounted) solar project and PM Kusum B project majorly as a site planning lead. This 
was an onsite role and it needed regular site visit in order to ensure all works were aligned as per work schedule and 
no site hindrance is hampering progress of work. 
 
Vendor Management & Quality Inspection: As this role included multiple projects so mapping vendors and 
tracking their progress was an exciting as well as challenging task. As a site planning lead, I was in regular 
communication with all the vendors as well as our site team which enabled an added advantage in terms of work 
efficiency. Inspecting the quality of work was also a dynamic job itself as it helped me to learn many things about 
site installation quality and correct way of implementing design at site. 
 
Material Planning & Resource Management: Optimized manpower and resources through strategic planning 
and coordination to meet site execution requirements. Coordinated with SCM team & procurement team to ensure 
timely dispatch & delivery of materials at site location.

OVERVIEW:Vehicle density refers to the number of vehicles present in a specific area. It is a factor considered in routing
protocols to determine the path selection for forwarding packets. Vehicle density plays a role in avoiding sparse and
disconnected areas, ensuring packets are forwarded to the most connected area with an adequate number of vehicles.
It is important to find a balance in vehicle density, as both low and high-density areas have their challenges - low
connectivity in sparse areas and congestion and potential packet drop or delay in high-density areas. The concept of
vehicle density helps improve forwarding decisions by prioritizing vehicles closer to the border in high-density areas.

CURRICULUM VITAE

Shivnandan Kumar Mahto

CAREER OBJECTIVE

Updating skills to deliver the best of my knowledge and professional work experience to the organization or place of work

RESUME SUMMERY:

More than 10 years of professional work experience in Civil Engineering (World Bank, AIIB & CTUIL) in the field of Power Transmission & Substation sector in Tamilnadu, Karnataka, Assam and Jharkhand state.

JOB PROFILE

Project Management Consultant of Total Civil Work for Transmission Line & Sub-Station.

Civil Drawing study and approval for 765/400/220/ 132/33KV Substation and Transmission line.

Construction supervision and preparation of MIS.

Detailed supervision as per FQP for Transmission Line & Sub-Station.

Civil related documents verification like Cube Test Report, Construction Material & Source approval.

Preparing feasibility reports, for Sub-Station and Transmission lines etc.

Preparation of DPR, MPR supporting to project team.

As site in charge taking care of Planning, Scheduling.

Coordinating between clients, contractor, regional office for progress of project, conducting daily, weekly, and monthly meetings with client, contractor and executing staff at site and review with designer at HO for problems resolution.

Checking the erection plans material availability as per AFC Drawings and QAP.

Conducting site inspections.

Job supervision of 765/400/220/132/33 KV Transmission Line & Sub-Station of civil portions. Like Power Transformer & Reactor Foundation, equipment foundation, Tower foundation, RCC road Bitumen road, Retaining Wall and residential buildings.

Verification of Joint Measurement sheet for Substation and Transmission Line.

Project Billing- (Clint/Contractor/Sub Contractor) like Erection, supply, Freight and PV Bill.

Monitoring compliance of contractor’s legal requirements.

Site audit to check civil compliance status of contractors as per project required.

Plan and organize works of civil construction including employee enforcement of construction procedures.

Check the compliance of work permit with the work methods.

Deal with client and consultant in the purpose of their requirements.

Provided necessary help to work force in maintaining good housekeeping & proper waste disposal.

EMPLOYMENT NARRATION:

Present Company

TATA CONSULTING ENGINEERS LIMITED.

July 2023 – Till Working as Independent Engineer Civil, for consultancy service under Central Transmission Utility of India Ltd (CTUIL) where looking 765 KV Transmission lines (320 KM New Narendra GIS To Pune GIS) with 765 KV GIS at Vijayapura (Karnataka) & Pune (Maharashtra).

PROJECT: - Engagement of Independent Engineer for transmission scheme under “ISTS Network Expansion scheme in Western Region & Southern Region for export of surplus power during high RE scenario in Southern Region” (Spec. No. CTUIL/IE/2022-23/05)

OWNER: - Central Transmission Utility of India Limited (CTUIL)

Developer/TSP:- WRSR POWER TRANSMISSION LIMITED

About Tata Consulting Engineers Limited.

Tata Consulting Engineers Limited is India’s leading infrastructure services company with interests across various sectors like transportation, energy, and urban infrastructure. It provides consulting, engineering, project management, operations, and EPC services for new and existing projects. Client: CTUIL

Previous Company

FEEDBACK INFRA PVT. LTD.

Jan 2020 – July 2023 – Worked as Assistant Manager Civil, for consultancy service under Jharkhand Urja Sancharan Nigam Ltd (JUSNL, Govt. of Jharkhand) and Assam Electricity Grid Corporation Ltd. (AEGCL, Govt. of Assam) where looking 132 KV Transmission lines (566.9 KM) with 132/33 KV sub-stations (12 No’s of new GSS and 4 No’s of Bay Extension) in World Bank and AIIB Project

PROJECT: - Jharkhand Power System Improvement Project. OWNER: - Jharkhand Urja Sancharan Nigam Limited.

About Feedbackinfra Pvt. Ltd.

Feedback Infra is India’s leading infrastructure services company with interests across various sectors like transportation, energy, and urban infrastructure. It provides consulting, engineering, project management, operations, and EPC services for new and existing projects. Client: JUSNL and AEGCL.

KEC INTERNATIONAL LTD.

Jan 2017 – Dec 2019 Worked as Site Engineer in 400/220/66 kV Substation at Hebbanahalli and 220/66/11 kV Substation at Chiknagra, Sakleshpur, Hassan District, Karnataka.

PROJECT: - Yettinahole Integrated Drinking Water Supply Project

OWNER: - VJNL

Previously worked 220/110/66/11 kV Bay extension at Hubbali, Dhār wad District, Karnataka and 220 kV D/C Transmission Line Maggadi to Biddadi at Maggadi, Ramnagar District, Karnataka. Client: KPTCL.

About KEC International Ltd.

Deliver projects in key infrastructure sectors such as Power Transmission & Distribution, Railways, Civil, Urban Infrastructure, Solar, Smart Infrastructure, and Cables.

S2P CONSTRUCTION.

Sep 2013 – Dec 2016 worked as Field Engineer, 220KV Transmission line, EPIP GIS to Yarrandahalli GSS at Bangalore, Karnataka. Client: KPTCL. Previously worked 400 kV Transmission Line at Chennai. Client: TNEB.

About S2P Construction.

Company Deals in execution work of various Transmission line and Substation.

ACHEIVMENT

07 no of GSS successfully charged

02 no of Bay Extension successfully charged

02 no of Transmission Line success fully charged

ACADEMIA

B. Tech in Civil Engineering (2013) from Cambridge Institute of Technology, Ranchi Jharkhand.

IT EXPOSURE

Well versed with M.S. Office (Word, Excel, Power Point)

PROFESSIONAL SKILLS

Good Communication & Negotiation Skills

Assertive and flexible nature.

Analytical and Problem-solving skills.

Have a good capability of handling contractors, local hindrances, and public litigations.

PERSONAL VITAE

Father’s Name : Ravi Shankar Mahto

Permanent Address : AT+ PO-Bhelwara, PS-Bishnugarh

Dist. - Hazaribag Jharkhand, Pin-825312

Date of Birth : 10-05-1991.

Languages Known : English, Hindi, Khortha, Nagpuri Bhojpuri and Kannada. Marital Status : Married

Driving License : Indian

Passport : Yes

I dream it a privilege to be an employee of your Organization I assure you that if appointed would do my best to raise to the expectation of my superior.

World Bank (WB) is supporting Jharkhand Urja Sancharan Nigam Limited (JUSNL) with a loan of 
US$310 million to achieve the ‘24/7 Power for All’ goal of the Government of the Jharkhand 
(GOJ). JUSNL is using the fund to construct substations and transmission lines to evacuate power from 
upcoming generation plants of 4.3 GW capacity and to support the availability of electricity in all 
corners of the state of Jharkhand. This World Bank Funded Transmission Project of JUSNL under 
JPSIP has been divided into 16 Packages, which includes 8 Nos of 132/33 Grid Substation 
Packages having capacity of 2*50 MVA each and 8 Nos of Transmission Lines Packages having 
total length of 2244 CKM. The overall project is divided into Package-1 as Zone-1 (Ranchi) & Zone-2 
(Dumka) and Package-2 as Zone-3 (Jamshedpur) and Zone-4 (Daltonganj) in Jharkhand District. 
 
M/s Feedback Infra Pvt. Ltd. has been appointed for Package-1. The scope of work is to deliver 
services for Transmission Projects consisting of 12 Grid Substations of 2X50 MVA capacity each and 
1030 CKM of 132 kV Transmission Lines. I was independently handling all the entire Electrical 
Execution including Testing and Commissioning with progress reports for Ranchi Zone (Irba, Angada & 
Silli GSS.

project and support the officials for its faster & quicker resolution.

GTP/MQP, vendor approvals and all site related activities. 
• Understanding of contracts and procurement in power sector, like TBCB tenders, other tender 
documents related to the project. 
• Accountable for attending progress review meetings with Client and Stake holders.

activities are conducted under controlled conditions as per drawings, specification, and work 
plan.

Planning, Approvals, and other Liaison works.

equipment’s up to 400 kV and teaming up with sub-contractors and clients and managing the 
entire project including billing. 
• Erection, Testing and Commissioning work of SF6 CB, CT, CVT, 11 KV HT ABC, XLPE CABLE, VCB 
Panel and Distribution Transformer etc. under DDUGJY scheme. 
• BOQ Preparation, Project Planning, Project execution, Quality Control, MIS preparation, 
Correspondence and Sub-Contractor Management and Billing. 
• Store Management, Material Planning, Store Audit, Contractor’s material reconciliation.

Executive Summary

T. A. Andre & Sons General Contractors (Ontario), Kingston, ON 2024

Project Coordinator

 Worked on renewable energy, commercial and non-commercial projects across South-East Ontario. Improved the overall process for change order and purchase order management. Also, improved the internal document coordination regarding billing and Time & Material sheets.

BASS Curtainwalls Inc., Toronto, ON 2023

Project Administrator Co-op

Direct the full administration for a commercial project (G+8) “Queen and Richmond Centre 2” valued at $15M. Scope projects, coordinate assets, and manage vendor relationships to meet pre-production, production, post-production, and on-site support targets. Draft reports and documentation in compliance with company and confidentiality guidelines. Resolve onsite issues arising amongst work teams. Track and monitor work progress generating project budget and productivity variance reports. Perform quality control inspections to ensure installation within defined tolerance limits to eliminate rework.

Developed and implemented cost-saving procurement strategies including streamlining communications through creating cost code cheat sheet for workforce optimization resulting in a 15% reduction in work expenses and contributing to overall project savings of $50k on a $1M installation labor contract.

Implemented a revised project scheduling system that resulted in a 20% reduction in project completion time. This was achieved through a meticulous analysis of workflow processes and the identification of bottlenecks, allowing for a more streamlined and efficient project timeline. As a result, the project was delivered ahead of schedule, meeting all quality standards, and saving an additional $60,000 in potential overhead costs.

Implemented a communication strategy that led to a 15% reduction in project delays and anticipated legal expenses by approximately $30,000 through strengthened relationships, improved coordination with contractors, and enhanced regulatory compliance.

SKYGRiD Construction Inc., Toronto, ON 2022

Construction Site Co-op

Manage project coordination and serve as the field engineer for the mixed-use tower project "The Rosedale" and "Canopy by Hilton," valued at $200 million and reaching G+56 levels. Oversaw all construction activities, as well as deficiency completion, customer care quality inspections, and testing procedures to minimize deficiencies and nonconformance. Prepared meeting minutes, requests for information, and other logs to facilitate better site coordination with appropriate stakeholders. Assembled relevant documentation pertaining to project occupancy ensuring compliance with City of Toronto guidelines. Validated change and work orders. Maintained a variety of current records inclusive of drawings, revision notices, and purchase and change orders across cross-functional teams consisting of suppliers, subcontractors, project developers, consultants, customer care staff, property managers, and other regulatory entities.

Enhanced the change order validation process by consolidating review procedures reducing average change order validation time by 25% due to faster approval and implementation resulting in at $500,000 cost savings.

Implemented a streamlined documentation workflow, reducing the time required to process requests for information and other logs by 20%. This efficiency improvement enhanced site coordination with stakeholders, contributing to a smoother project execution and minimizing delays. The streamlined process not only saved time but also improved overall project communication.

Enhanced deficiency completion and testing procedures, resulting in a 15% reduction in post-construction deficiencies and nonconformance issues. By implementing more rigorous quality inspections and testing protocols, the project achieved higher standards of construction quality, reducing the need for rework and customer care interventions. This improvement not only increased customer satisfaction but also saved an estimated $50,000 in post-construction corrective measures.

New Tayler, Glass, Doors & Metal Inc., Chicago, IL 2020 – 2021

Project Estimator

Led the full estimation function of multiple non-union glazing projects in the US. Estimated material take-offs for storefronts, curtain walls, doors, and windows. Requested material quotes from preferred vendors. Integrated tender requests with shop drawings, cost estimates, and competitive bid packages with comprehensive bid price tender proposals. Collaborated with the project team on project updates, RFIs, and scope changes.

Successfully refined the estimating process of new software solutions implementations increasing project bid accuracy, leading to 15% lift in win rate, and generating $1.5M in incremental revenue

Implemented a vendor negotiation strategy that resulted in a 10% reduction in material costs for glazing projects. By fostering stronger relationships with key suppliers and negotiating favorable terms, the cost savings directly contributed to project profitability. This optimization in vendor relationships also ensured a more competitive edge in pricing during the bidding process, resulting in an additional $800,000 in overall project savings.

Spearheaded a value engineering initiative that reduced project costs by 12% without compromising quality. Collaborated with the engineering and design teams to identify alternative materials and construction methods that maintained project specifications while achieving substantial cost savings. This strategic approach not only increased the competitiveness of bids but also resulted in a direct cost reduction of $1.2 million across a portfolio of non-union glazing projects.

Additional Experience:

Project Engineer Intern, Simplex Infrastructures Ltd, Mumbai, India, 2018 – 2019

A project trainee working on a large-scale infrastructure ($600 million) elevated metro project, a 16.475km long stretch from Andheri (E) to Dahisar with 13 Elevated stations. Planning and tracking construction progress (planned against actual) using MS Excel and maintaining administrative documentation such as purchase orders, material logs, equipment logs, etc. Created detailed activity reports including material consumption calculations, equipment owning and operating costs, time cycle and labor productivity analysis for substructure and superstructure elements such as U-girders, I-girders, piers, pile foundations, and pile caps.

Field Engineer Trainee, Takshshila AIR, Ahmedabad, India, 2017

Field Engineer Trainee, D.S. Associates, Gandhinagar, India, 2016 

A field engineer trainee working on a residential twin tower project ($50 million, G+25) and composite bungalow structure ($50 million, comprising 25 units of G+2). Monitored construction processes, drafted progress reports, labor productivity, and time cycle analyses. Generated unit cost estimation for different construction elements like beams, columns, and slabs. Assessed ownership and operating expenses of tools and machinery used during the construction phase. Enhanced understanding of construction processes and contributed to efficient project cost analysis, improving overall decision-making.

Accomplished Project Management Head with 13 years of experience, mostly in the renewable 
energy industry, specializing in project execution, technical management, and safety operations. 
Adept at integrating cutting-edge management technologies and processes to drive organizational 
improvements and compliance with regulatory standards. Committed to utilizing leadership and 
skills to contribute positively to organizational goals while promoting continuous learning and 
innovation.

Project Management Head | Ecoteq Green Energies Foundation Mar 2024 – Present

 Collaborate with the design engineering team to prepare and validate proposals and Return 
on Investment (ROI) calculations

Materials (BOM) was practical and executable 
 
Senior Manager - Project | Solace Renewable Energy Pvt. Ltd. Dec 2022 – Feb 2024

meetings, and overseeing the preparation of technical and commercial calculations

closure meetings

departments to ensure timely material delivery

execution and incidental expenditures 
 Enhanced client communications, facilitated inter-departmental coordination, and 
maintained project schedules with Gantt chart management

payment follow-ups

service audits, and attended service review meetings

performance tracking, and appraisals

O&M Manager

 Resolved inverter technical issues and managed datalogger installations and servicing

 Oversaw the transition of plant operations from project development to ongoing maintenance 
 
Manager, Projects | Punam Energy Pvt. Ltd. June 2017 – Mar 2020 
 Managed solar power plant installations and commissioning for high-profile clients like Coal India, SBI, and GE 
 Led the development and management of Installation & Commissioning (I&C) vendor, OEM vendors and Client relationships

IOCL, HPCL, and BPCL

Operations Head (North)

 Coordinated daily complaint logging, resolution and escalation processes, maintaining high standards of service with IOCL, HPCL, and BPCL

Service Coordinator for the Eastern region 
 Led a team of 40 service engineers across 11 states, efficiently managing service escalations and maintaining high standards

Name of assignment or project: Rahughat Hydro-Electric Project (40 MW), Beni, Myagdi District, Nepal 

Year: From April 2021 to till date

Location: Nepal

Main project features: Raghuganga Hydropower Limited (RGHPL) was established in 2017 March with an aim of power generation of 40 MW in Gandaki Province of Myagdi District, Nepal. Nepal Electricity Authority (NEA) own cent percent share of this project. EXIM bank of India has provide the soft loan for this projects.

The annual energy generation from the plant is about 247.89 GWh, of which 137.71GWh is firm energy in 90 % dependable year

Positions held: Civil Manager

Activities performed:

Settlement of Camp and procurement of boat and other necessary material

Oversee excavation, foundation preparation, concrete pouring, and reinforcement work for key structures such as dams, powerhouses, tunnels, and penstocks.

Ensure alignment, leveling, and proper execution of civil structures according to design drawings.

Supervise the installation of hydraulic structures such as spillways, weirs, surge shafts, and intake structures

Quality Control and of execution of Systematic Geo Bag and GI wire netting boxes filled with sand filled geobags laying by boat/without boat and recording of daily progress report for client submission.

Continuously tracking project expenses against the budget.

Earth work in Recoupment bank embankment and trimming to the design section/slope including removing the soils and depositing on bank.

Identifying areas of potential cost savings and recommending adjustments.

Preparation of labour, machinery and client bill.

Name of assignment or project: Arun-III Hydroelectric Project (900 MW) Nepal.

Year: From Oct 2018 to Jul 2021

Location: Koshi, Nepal

Procuring agency or Client: SJVN

Main project features: The project consists of a 70m high, 466m wide concrete gravity dam across the Arun River which will be able to store 13.94 million cubic meters of water. The dam will have six (now only five) sluice gates. There will be four underground desolating basins (they have since been removed from the proposal) having a length of 420m, a width of 16m and a height of 24m each. A 9.5m diameter tunnel having length of 11.74 km followed by 9.5m diameter two steel-lined pressure shafts and four penstocks will convey the flow to the powerhouse. 

Positions held: Quantity Surveyor

Activities performed:

Safety equipment install and monitoring in tunnel for construction of Cut off wall works and coordinating with special subcontractor Soletanche Bachy France.

Identifying areas of potential cost savings and recommending adjustments.

Execution and supervision of site works as per the approved plans and drawing

Preparation Monthly and yearly budget and program and material requisition and procurement.

Preparing detailed cost estimates for the entire hydroelectric project, including civil works (dams, tunnels, spillways) and mechanical/electrical installations.

Creating and managing project budgets to avoid cost overruns.

Continuously tracking project expenses against the budget.

Work includes construction of Cut of wall works and Dam pier, trunnion and Brest wall works.

Co-ordination with senior management and client regarding progress, quality and safety of work.

Accountable for project management and control at HQ level

Successfully obtained Extension of Time(EOT) for the project

Planning and Scheduling of Project.

Name of assignment or project: Mangdehuu Hydroelectric Project (720 MW) Bhutan Year: April 2014 to Sep 2018

Location: Trongsa Dzongkhag District, central Bhutan

Procuring agency or Client: Govt of Bhutan

Main project features: The Mangdechhu run-of-river hydroelectric power plant has a 101.5m-high concrete gravity dam from the deepest foundation level, two intake tunnels, measuring 196m and 150m-long respectively and a horseshoe-shaped 13.54km-long headrace tunnel with a 6.5m diameter. The tunnel can discharge 118m³ of water a second.

The 152m-high surge shaft has a diameter of 13.5m. Water is fed to the underground powerhouse through two steel-lined pressure shafts that are 1,853m and 3.5m-long in diameter.

Positions held: Civil Engineer & Quantity surveyor

Activities performed:

Conduct on-site testing of concrete, aggregates, soil, and steel reinforcements to ensure compliance with project standards.

Inspect formwork, scaffolding, and reinforcement placement before concrete pouring.

Verify the proper curing of concrete to avoid structural defects.

Ensure earthwork compaction and slope stabilization in dam embankments and tunnel linings.

Conduct regular safety briefings and toolbox talks for site workers.

Implement safety measures like protective barriers, proper scaffolding, and hazard signs.

Ensure compliance with local, national, and international construction standards (e.g., FERC, BIS, IS Codes, World Bank guidelines).

Ensure proper sediment control, drainage, and water diversion during construction.

Monitor water levels, flood risks, and spillway efficiency to maintain safety.

Implement erosion control measures and follow environmental best practices.

Preparing detailed cost estimates for the entire hydroelectric project, including civil works (dams, tunnels, spillways) and mechanical/electrical installations.

Creating and managing project budgets to avoid cost overruns.

Continuously tracking project expenses against the budget.

Name of assignment or project: Jaypee Nigri Thermal Power Plant (1320MW) MP Year: April 2012 to April 2014

Location: Nigari

Seasoned Transmission & Power Sector expert with more than 32 years of extensive experience and demonstrated history in Transmission Planning for National Grid, Renewable generation, development of regulatory regime including connectivity/LTA/GNA for conventional as well as renewable generation, Commercial, Regulatory, Policy, Legal, Contractual, Sectoral Reforms, Business Strategy & Development and Project Management side in Transmission Sector. Strategized/ led /part of Policy making in key Sectoral reforms beginning from separation of Transmission to introduction of Open Access, Electricity Act 2003, Tariff Policy, NEP, ISTS planning, Private participation in ISTS, Regulations and procedures for LTA/MTOA & GNA grant, processing of connectivity/LTA applications and Calculation and Sharing of ISTS charges. 

Managed Revenue Assurance, Commercial Agreements, Tariff Petitions, Regulatory and Legal matters, Dispute resolution, Court cases, Regulatory petition management, License & approval for new business, Contractual & Commercial transaction, Project Management and Stakeholder Consultation.

Leader with motivational management style & reputation for building and retaining highly motivated teams.

Successfully handled critical litigations and disputes in APTEL/High Courts/Supreme Courts to end long pending issues mainly related to Outstanding Dues, Mismatch issues, Tariff disputes. 

Led team for grant of Regulatory approvals for Transmission projects for Renewables Generation, and Solar Power parks in India, High Capacity Corridors, New Business initiatives. 

Engineer to Chief General Manager, CTU Aug’91 to Sep’20

Responsible for/Worked on

Development of regulatory procedures for connectivity / LTA / GNA for various entities like conventional/renewable generations, consumers, DISCOMs etc. Handled processing and grant of Long Term Access, Connectivity applications as per CERC regulations since 2004 till 2020. 

Planning of reliable & techno economic transmission schemes for evacuation of power from various Thermal, Hydro and renewable generations in coordination with CEA, STUs, RPCs etc.

Introduction and adoption of various new technologies like Series Reactor, Series Capacitors, TCSC, STATCOMs, 800 kV HVDC system etc. in the country.

Project completed after joining in the Service since Graduation in Engineering:-
TRANSMISSION LINE PROJECT: COMPLETED & COMMISSIONED over 4500 ckt. Km of EHV Transmission lines of 132 KV HVAC to ±800 KV HVDC.
SUBSTATIONS: COMPLETED & COMMISSIONED 17 AIS & GIS substations from 132 KV to 400 KV substations with over 1200 MVA Transformation capacity spreading over all the seven states of NER i.e. ASSAM, MANIPUR, NAGALAND, MIZORAM, TRIPURA, ARUNACHAL PRADESH & MEGHALAYA.. Alongwith the completion of the EHV Substations the associated Resendential complexes were and the Colonies were completed.

132 KV TRANSMISSION SCHEME from OTPC's 726 MW GBPP, Tripura from Palatana to SM NAGAR.

220 KV LINES from Mariani Assam to Mokokchung, Nagaland, 400 KV Silchar-Imphal and 400 KV PK Bari, Tripura to Silchar, Assam lines have been completed recently for evacuation of share of power of OTPC's 726 MW GBPP, Tripura and NTPC's 750 MW Thermal Power Project, Kokrajhar distt, Assam to Nagaland and Assam.

±800 KV 6000 MW HVDC bi-pole Transmission line from Biswanath Chariali, Assam to AGRA ( UPTO Baroboisa, West Bengal ) under completion for evacuation of 2000 MW( Ist phase) Power from Lower Subansiri HEP, Arunachal Pradesh.

132 KV Pasighat-Roing-Tezu-Namsai line for evacuation of share of power from OTPC's 726 MW GBPP, Tripura and NTPC's 750 MW Thermal Power Project, Kokrajhar distt, Assam to Arunachal Pradesh. 
In addition to above major projects, several EHV missing link projects spread over all the states in NER were executed during the period.
